title: Complexity pair entry
description: One entry of the complexity-pairs dataset. See START_HERE.txt sections 1-3 for the meaning of every field.

id.description: Stable slug; must equal the entry's folder name.

problem_statement.description: What is computed, unambiguously, for ALL input sizes n.

input.description: What n is, and how input size is measured.

size_measure.description: How the input size relates to n (e.g. 'n bits', 'n vertices, Theta(n^2) matrix entries').

secondary_tags.description: Optional extra tags; the primary tag is pair_type and must not be repeated here.

relationship.description: Which algorithm improves which, and in what measure.

proofs.description: Citations of complexity proofs (required for V3). Indexes into sources[] or free-text references.

test_harness.description: Required for V1+. A Python module (path relative to the entry folder) exposing generate(n, rng) and optionally check(instance, output), equal(a, b), generate_scaling(n, rng), reported_cost(output).

provenance.description: Whose result the entry is (optional; absent means 'literature'). 'literature': the result is in the cited literature and was re-proved or re-checked here. 'own': no prior literature was found after a documented search. 'own-extension': an own generalization or sharpening of the cited base result(s). 'pending': an inaccessible source might already cover the result (see pending_note).

bases.description: Citations of the base result(s); required for 'own-extension'.

proof.description: Present only when every claim of this item has a complete written proof by this project in the repository, and deterministic checks re-run the proofs' computable facts. Shown as the green check mark (✅ Proved). External citations are credit, not part of the proof. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

documents.description: Files, relative to this item's folder, that hold the written proofs of all its claims.

checks.description: Deterministic scripts or tests, relative to this item's folder, that re-check the proofs' computable facts.

audit.description: The RESEARCH_LOG entry that records the claim-by-claim audit behind the mark.

lower_bounds.description: Known lower bounds for the problem. Required (with a classical model) for T9.

pair_type.description: T1 exp->poly; T2 naive-exp->poly; T3 poly->faster poly; T4 randomized<->deterministic; T5 quantum->classical (dequantization); T6 open/unpaired; T7 synthetic/bloated; T8 super-poly->faster super-poly; T9 quantum separation in a query/oracle/black-box model (classical lower bound cited or proved in the entry).

model.description: Computational model. Lets the dataset be queried for classical-vs-quantum questions.

time_complexity.description: In terms of n as defined in input.parameter.

implementation.description: 'relative/path.py:function_name' (relative to the entry folder), or null.

harness.description: How the validator exercises this implementation.

v1_max_n.description: Largest n this implementation is run on during V1 (keeps slow algorithms tractable).

scaling.description: V2 check: fit log(measured) = alpha * log(cost(n)) + c over n_values and require |alpha - 1| <= tolerance. measured is wall-clock time (measure='time') or an operation count the implementation reports (measure='reported', e.g. oracle queries; needs harness.reported_cost). A constant cost expression is checked as max/min of the measured values <= 1 + tolerance.

cost.description: Claimed cost as an arithmetic expression in n. Allowed: + - * / **, numbers, n, e, pi, phi, log, log2, sqrt, exp, factorial.

samples.description: Instances averaged per n (use > 1 for randomized algorithms).

rivals.description: Cost expressions the measurement must NOT fit (|alpha - 1| > tolerance). Makes V2 discriminating: e.g. Strassen claims n**log2(7) and lists n**3 as a rival.

shape.description: Optional and informational (never changes a V2 verdict): exact shape diagnostic for exact counts (measure 'reported'). The counts are computed on a regular grid, a recurrence is guessed (overdetermined, one-dimensional solution space, held-out terms reproduced) and its dominant root and exponent are compared exactly with the shape of `cost` (C * b^n * n^p * (log n)^q). A consecutive grid sees b and p; a doubling grid (n = 2^k) sees p and q. See notes/v2-shape-diagnostic.md.

sequence.description: 'consecutive': n = lo, lo+step, ..., hi; 'doubling': n = lo, 2 lo, 4 lo, ..., hi (powers of two).

n_range.description: [lo, hi], inclusive. At most 64 grid points.

step.description: Consecutive grids only: spacing of n (must divide lo). The recurrence is guessed in t = n/step.

max_degree.description: Largest coefficient degree of a polynomial-coefficient (P-recursive) recurrence tried.

holdout.description: Held-out terms the guess must reproduce (default 4 for constant coefficients, 3 for polynomial coefficients; never below 2). Recorded with the result.

python_version_dependent.description: True if the count includes work inside CPython built-ins (sorted, min, max, ...), which may differ between Python versions (RL-069). The result is then UNDETERMINED (python_version_dependent); what was found is still recorded.

expect.description: Explicit claimed shape, used instead of parsing `cost` (e.g. when cost uses a decimal approximation of an algebraic base).

base.description: Exponential base b: an exact constant expression ('phi', '3 + 2*sqrt(2)'), or {minpoly: integer coefficients highest degree first, approx: a number that singles out the real root}. Default '1'.

polynomial_factor.description: Exponent p of n: rational or rational + log2(exact constant), e.g. '-1/2', 'log2(7)'. Default '0'.

log_power.description: Exponent q of log n (rational). Default 0.

note.description: Free text, e.g. why this grid was chosen.

model.description: A bound for classical-randomized also holds for classical-deterministic.

setting.description: e.g. 'unconditional', 'query (oracle) model', 'generic group model', 'conditional on SETH'
